title: IFC carries the semantics in BIM; DWG is a non-semantic derivative generated from 3D models
content:
DWG files are building/construction CAD files **without semantic meaning** — these days typically generated from RVT or IFC files as 2D drawings, cuts, and projections. IFC is the BIM standard for 3D construction files **with semantic meaning**; Autodesk Revit's RVT is the most common proprietary 3D format.

The industry is mid-transition: from 2D-DWG-first workflows to building 3D BIM models first and deriving 2D plans from them, so that elements — a door, a duct — carry semantic tags rather than being anonymous line work (DT BAU walkthrough, 00:11:26–00:14:11).

Two practical consequences:
- DWG survives as an interchange and precise-measurement format, not as the source of truth.
- The construction toolchain is 90–95% Windows because Revit and most industry tools lack Mac support; Mac-based architecture studios fall back to DWG interchange to participate (00:35:39).

Semantic 3D-first modeling is what makes model data machine-readable at all — every automation ambition downstream (collision checks, AI review, structured BCF workflows) depends on it.
description: DWG files are 2D CAD without semantic meaning, today generated from RVT/IFC. IFC is the semantic BIM standard; the industry builds 3D-first and derives plans from models.
